title: How and why Fats formed his big band
summary: Booking dance halls required more than six men, so Fats augmented the group with extra sax, trombone and trumpet players for three or four years of one-nighters.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: I'm glad you mentioned the big band, Herman. How did the big band happen to come into existence? Why was the big band, since you'd been doing so well with the small group?

Well, here's what happened. The bookings, because we were playing here, and playing there, and the bookings came up and then people asking, we would like to have Fats Waller and his band play a dance here and a dance there. Well, you can't send six men out to play a hall where you'd been having fifteen, twenty men playing. You know, and make everybody happy. So, they told them, say okay, I'll

augment the band, get some pieces, get some other guys. So Fats had Don, other guys, to hire five, six saxophone players, two, three trombones, two three trumpets, you know. Pick the band, and get some arrangements, and rehearses, and they make it, you know, and take it on the job. That's what we did.
Oh, aw, we did one nighters, oh, two, three, three or four years.
Well, it's like he stopped, and the bookings stopped, and he stopped, and he didn't want to do them anymore, maybe. You know.
Was the big band as successful as the small group, from an audience response?
I think so. Oh, heck yeah. He could have gone on, but he's a small, big, he could -- but evidently he didn't want -- he -- you know.
